title: The Definite Article
subtitle: il, lo, la, l', i, gli, le — the six forms of the.
objectives: Learn the six forms of the definite article.
Apply the initial-sound rule: il before most consonants, lo before s+consonant/z/gn/ps, l' before vowels.
Form the plural: i, gli, le.

sections.heading: Why six forms?
sections.body: English has one form of the definite article: the. Italian has six: il, lo, la, l', i, gli, le. The form depends on two things: the gender of the noun (masculine or feminine) and the initial sound of the following word. Masculine singular: il (before most consonants), lo (before s+consonant, z, gn, ps, x, y), l' (before a vowel). Feminine singular: la (before consonants), l' (before a vowel). Masculine plural: i (il becomes i), gli (lo becomes gli, l' becomes gli). Feminine plural: le (la becomes le, l' becomes le).

rows: i libri, gli studenti, gli uomini

sections.heading: From Manzoni
sections.body: Alessandro Manzoni, I promessi sposi: Quel ramo del lago di Como. il lago (the lake): masculine, singular, before l (a liquid consonant, so il). Boccaccio, Decameron: Umana cosa è aver compassione degli afflitti. degli afflitti: degli is a contraction of di + gli (of the afflicted, masculine plural). We will cover contractions in a later lesson.
